src/linearize.jl:357-369 loops `for group in Iterators.partition(1:N, width)`. It reads x rows with `for (i, (_, entry)) in enumerate(x_entries)` and `_readback!(A, B, i, _read(entry, seeded_exec), group, n_x)` (:363-364). The entry is the DerivRead half of an `(site, DerivRead)` pair, and `_read` takes the executor itself (src/readers.jl:590). `_readback!` (linearize.jl:578-586) fills only the group's columns. No `ẋbuf_at` exists in src/, and `git log -S'ẋbuf_at'` finds only c347a010, the walkthrough's own commit. The grouped loop has been there since the first code commit, 4f795b30, which predates the walkthrough's promotion. No record covers the full-column sketch.
judgments.fix:
for group in Iterators.partition(1:N, width)        # one evaluation per group of `width` directions
    # seed the group's sites, then evaluate!(exec)
    for (i, (_, entry)) in enumerate(x_entries)      # rows of A and B; entry is the DerivRead
        ẋ₀[i] = _readback!(A, B, i, _read(entry, exec), group, n_x)
    end
    for (i, entry) in enumerate(y_entries)           # rows of C and D
        y₀[i] = Float64(_readback!(C, D, i, _read(entry, exec), group, n_x))
    end
end
# _readback! writes partial `pos` of the group's direction k into A/C (k ≤ n_x) or B/D (k > n_x)
judgments.note: D-272 backs the code's grouping, which the walkthrough's own section 7 describes. No entry backs the doc's full-column loop. Writing the sketch with or without the `_readback!` helper are both faithful, so the fix is not unique.
